submission.natural_language_explanation: L11/N468+ is a retrospective specialist-content detector: it fires on scientific, medical and technical vocabulary - the specialist word itself, one of its sub-word pieces, or the compound term it heads (immune, genetic, molecular, cognitive, synaptic, enzyme, protein, cell, DNA, Pleistocene, gas giant, chemical energy) - at 0.7-2.2 (0.3-1.0 of the scan maximum), and it also fires at 0.9-2.1, with the peak on the auxiliary, on reported-statement clauses that have a person-noun subject ('the senator announced she was late', 'the mayor said she would attend', 'my sister announced she was engaged'). It stays near zero (0.19-0.45, at most 0.2 of maximum) on ordinary prose built from frequent words ('the cat sat on the mat', 'the weather was mild all week'), on institutional, legal or business prose that carries no specialist term ('the parliament ratified the treaty', 'the court convicted the defendant'), on a specialist word used in an ordinary predicative sense ('she was immune to the criticism', 0.38), and on generic-subject reported clauses ('the teacher said she would be late', 0.34).
